content:
We need to find a template that when applied retrosynthetically (i.e., reverse of forward) reproduces the reaction: cycloaddition forming a ring, forming C-C bond, breaking C-O bond, losing ketones and C-C triple bonds functional groups. The target molecule is given: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O

We need to search template catalog with criteria: functional groups broken in forward reaction: carbon-oxygen bond broken (so C-O broken). functional groups formed in forward: ketones and C-C triple bonds are lost (so they are present in reactants but not in product). Actually forward reaction loses ketones and C-C triple bonds, meaning those groups are present in starting materials and disappear in product. So in retrosynthesis, we need to add them back: we need to find a template where in forward direction, a ketone and a C-C triple bond are formed? Wait: forward reaction loses ketones and C-C triple bonds, meaning they are present in reactants and not in product. So in retrosynthetic direction (going from product to precursors), we need to generate precursors that contain a ketone and a C-C triple bond. Also forward reaction forms a C-C bond (new sigma) and breaks a C-O bond. So in retrosynthesis, we need to break a C-C bond and form a C-O bond.

Thus we need to search templates with functional groups broken: C-C bond formed forward => broken backward, so we need template where C-C bond is broken in forward? Actually forward forms C-C, so forward bond formed list includes C-C. So we can set bonds_formed: "C-C". Also forward breaks C-O, so bonds_broken: "C-O". Functional groups formed forward: none? Actually ketones and C-C triple bonds are lost, so they are not formed. So functional groups broken forward: ketone and C-C triple bond? Wait they are lost, meaning they are present in reactants and disappear, so they are broken (i.e., functional groups broken). So functional groups broken: "ketones", "C-C triple bonds". So we can set functional_groups_broken accordingly.

Let's get list of available functional groups to ensure naming.
